# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70700> (open access; Data S1 holds the
  covariate equations, the second supplement Figures S1-S31 and their
  regression footnotes, the third Tables S1-S4)

Shahraz 2026 reports a pooled population PK model for savolitinib, a selective
MET tyrosine-kinase inhibitor, and uses its individual exposures in a set of
logistic exposure-response analyses. The paper contributes seven models:

| Model | What it is | Driver |
|-------|------------|--------|
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib` | One-compartment popPK with a depot and two transit compartments | dose |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_allcomers` | Objective response, SAVANNAH all comers without prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy (Figure 3a) | `CTROUGH` |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_highmet` | Objective response, high MET biomarker without prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy (Figure 3b) | `CTROUGH` |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_lowmet` | Objective response, low MET biomarker without prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy (Figure 3c) | `CTROUGH` |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_highmet_2l` | Objective response, high MET biomarker in second line (Figure 3d) | `CTROUGH` |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc` | 23 adverse-event logistic regressions (Figures 5a, 5c, S11a-S31a) | `AUC_SAVOLITINIB` |
| `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_cmax` | 22 adverse-event logistic regressions (Figures 5b, 5d, S11b-S31b) | `CMAX` |

The exposure-response models carry no PK layer: the exposure is a column the
user supplies, usually derived from the popPK model as shown below.

# Population

The popPK analysis pooled 998 patients and 9706 plasma concentrations from 10
phase I-III studies (Table S1) of savolitinib alone (40.9%) or with osimertinib
80 mg once daily (59.1%), at 100-1000 mg once daily or 100-600 mg twice daily.
Patients had locally advanced or metastatic solid tumours, mostly EGFR-mutated
MET-altered non-small cell lung cancer after osimertinib (SAVANNAH, TATTON),
papillary renal cell carcinoma, and NSCLC with MET exon 14 alterations. Median
age was 63 years (range 23-92), median weight 62.2 kg (36.0-177); 48.5% were
female; 55.7% were Asian, 40.5% White, 1.4% Black and 2.4% Other; 38.0% took a
proton pump inhibitor (Tables S2 and S3). The exposure-safety analyses used the
same 998 patients. The exposure-efficacy analyses used 360 SAVANNAH patients,
excluding the 24 on savolitinib plus placebo; Figure 3 reports 87 to 261
patients per subgroup.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The popPK
values:

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| `lka` (KA, all three absorption steps) | log(2.64) 1/h | Table 1 theta1; Figure S3 (Tr0 -> Tr1 -> Tr2 -> central, each at KA) |
| `lvc` (V/F) | log(173) L | Table 1 theta2 |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | log(31.7) L/h | Table 1 theta3 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.364 on (WT/62.2) | Table 1 theta6; Data S1 Vd/F equation |
| `e_alp_vc`, `e_alp_cl` | -0.0866, -0.0932 on (ALP/89) | Table 1 theta23, theta24; Data S1 |
| `e_tbili_cl` | -0.118 on (TBILI/8.5) | Table 1 theta8; Data S1 |
| `e_conmed_osimertinib_cl` | 0.119 | Table 1 theta10 (COMB); Data S1 |
| `e_sexf_vc`, `e_sexf_cl` | -0.160, -0.197 | Table 1 theta11, theta12; Data S1; Figure 2 labels SEX = 1 female |
| `e_race_white_vc`, `_cl`, `_ka` | 0.198, 0.212, 0.326 | Table 1 theta13, theta16, theta19; Data S1; Figure 2 labels RACE = 1 White |
| `e_conmed_ppi_vc`, `e_conmed_ppi_ka` | 0.0981, -0.164 | Table 1 theta9, theta22; Data S1 |
| `etalka`, `etalvc`, `etalcl` | 0.435, 0.0560, 0.135 | Table 1 Omega(1,1)-(3,3) |
| `addSd` | 1.07 ng/mL | Table 1 theta4 (err_add) |
| `propSd` | 0.495 | Table 1 theta5 (err_prop) |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | ng/mL | dose in mg, V/F in L |

The four ORR models are digitised from the Figure 3 curves; the paper prints no
ORR coefficients.

# Population PK

## Typical-value covariate effects (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the steady-state AUC24,ss, Cmax,ss and Cmin,ss of a patient at
the 10th and 90th percentile of each continuous covariate, or in each category,
relative to the reference patient (62.2 kg, ALP 89 U/L, bilirubin 8.5 umol/L,
male, non-White, no osimertinib, no PPI). The figure does not state the regimen;
300 mg twice daily reproduces all three metrics, and the AUC ratios do not
depend on the regimen.

```{r fig2}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib")
ref <- data.frame(
  WT = 62.2, ALP = 89, TBILI = 8.5, SEXF = 0, RACE_WHITE = 0,
  CONMED_OSIMERTINIB = 0, CONMED_PPI = 0
)
scenarios <- list(
  "WT 85.43 kg (q90)" = list(WT = 85.43), "WT 47.47 kg (q10)" = list(WT = 47.47),
  "BBILI 14 umol/L (q90)" = list(TBILI = 14), "BBILI 4.9877 umol/L (q10)" = list(TBILI = 4.9877),
  "BALP 217.3 U/L (q90)" = list(ALP = 217.3), "BALP 53 U/L (q10)" = list(ALP = 53),
  "With osimertinib" = list(CONMED_OSIMERTINIB = 1), "White" = list(RACE_WHITE = 1),
  "PPI" = list(CONMED_PPI = 1), "Female" = list(SEXF = 1)
)
# Figure 2a-c medians, in the order of `scenarios`
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~auc, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "WT 85.43 kg (q90)", 1.00, 0.946, 1.14,
  "WT 47.47 kg (q10)", 1.00, 1.05, 0.878,
  "BBILI 14 umol/L (q90)", 1.06, 1.03, 1.14,
  "BBILI 4.9877 umol/L (q10)", 0.938, 0.969, 0.862,
  "BALP 217.3 U/L (q90)", 1.09, 1.08, 1.10,
  "BALP 53 U/L (q10)", 0.953, 0.955, 0.947,
  "With osimertinib", 0.893, 0.947, 0.765,
  "White", 0.827, 0.874, 0.771,
  "PPI", 1.00, 0.924, 1.16,
  "Female", 1.24, 1.22, 1.32
)

ss_metrics <- function(params) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 300, ii = 12, addl = 49, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(576, 600, by = 0.05), cmt = "central")
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, ev, params = params, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
  s <- s[s$time >= 576 & s$time <= 600, ]
  data.frame(
    auc = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2),
    cmax = max(s$Cc), cmin = min(s$Cc)
  )
}
base <- ss_metrics(ref)
fig2 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(scenarios), function(nm) {
  p <- ref
  p[names(scenarios[[nm]])] <- unlist(scenarios[[nm]])
  m <- ss_metrics(p)
  data.frame(scenario = nm, auc_sim = m$auc / base$auc, cmax_sim = m$cmax / base$cmax, cmin_sim = m$cmin / base$cmin)
})) |>
  left_join(published, by = "scenario")
stopifnot(nrow(fig2) == length(scenarios), !anyNA(fig2))

fig2 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "AUC ratio (model)" = auc_sim, "AUC ratio (Fig 2a)" = auc,
    "Cmax ratio (model)" = cmax_sim, "Cmax ratio (Fig 2b)" = cmax,
    "Cmin ratio (model)" = cmin_sim, "Cmin ratio (Fig 2c)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value steady-state exposure ratios, 300 mg twice daily, vs Shahraz 2026 Figure 2.")

# Deterministic typical-value solve against two-to-three-digit printed values.
# The AUC ratio is exactly 1 / (CL multiplier), so it tests every CL term and
# both category codings (SEX = 1 female, RACE = 1 White); Cmax and Cmin add
# the V/F and KA terms. Achieved maximum differences: 0.005, 0.006 and 0.006.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(fig2$auc_sim - fig2$auc)) < 0.01,
  max(abs(fig2$cmax_sim - fig2$cmax)) < 0.012,
  max(abs(fig2$cmin_sim - fig2$cmin)) < 0.012
)
```

## Virtual cohort

The cohort mirrors the pooled demographics: log-normal weight, bilirubin and
alkaline phosphatase matched to the pooled median and interquartile range of
Table S2, and Bernoulli sex, race, PPI use and osimertinib co-administration at
the Table S3 proportions. Three regimens of 200 patients each cover the doses
of interest of the exposure-response analyses.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(70700)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(70700)
n_per_arm <- 200
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~amt, ~ii, ~daily,
  "300 mg QD", 300, 24, 300,
  "600 mg QD", 600, 24, 600,
  "300 mg BID", 300, 12, 600
)
# sdlog from the IQR: log(Q3 / Q1) / 1.349 (Table S2 pooled column)
make_cohort <- function(reg, id_offset) {
  covs <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    regimen = reg$regimen,
    daily_dose = reg$daily,
    WT = 62.2 * exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, log(73.6 / 54.0) / 1.349)),
    TBILI = 8.45 * exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, log(10.7 / 6.00) / 1.349)),
    ALP = 89 * exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, log(128 / 67.3) / 1.349)),
    SEXF = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.485),
    RACE_WHITE = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.405),
    CONMED_PPI = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.380),
    CONMED_OSIMERTINIB = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.591)
  )
  n_dose <- 240 / reg$ii
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(covs, time = seq(0, by = reg$ii, length.out = n_dose)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = reg$amt, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(covs, time = c(0, seq(216, 240, by = 0.25))) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(regimens[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(events$id)) == 3 * n_per_arm)
```

## Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_pk, events,
  keep = c("regimen", "daily_dose"), returnType = "data.frame"
)
sim_day10 <- sim |> filter(time >= 216)
```

```{r fig1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# In the spirit of Figure 1 / Figure S1: day-10 profiles by regimen, with the
# 17.3 ng/mL IC95 of phosphorylated MET.
sim_day10 |>
  mutate(tad = time - 216) |>
  group_by(regimen, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17.3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the day-10 morning dose (h)", y = "Savolitinib (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentile of 200 virtual patients per regimen; dashed: IC95 17.3 ng/mL."
  )
```

## PKNCA validation against Table S4

Table S4 summarises the model-predicted AUC24,ss, Cmax,ss and Cmin,ss of all
998 patients by most prevalent regimen. The simulated day-10 values (steady
state; the half-life is about 4 h) are compared with its medians.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time == 0 | time >= 216) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, Cc)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, amt)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 216, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
table_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~auclast, ~cmin,
  "300 mg QD", 1376, 8829, 13,
  "600 mg QD", 2444, 18354, 52,
  "300 mg BID", 1346, 16220, 167
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca, reference = table_s4, by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated day-10 medians vs Shahraz 2026 Table S4 medians (AUC over",
    "24 h, i.e. two intervals for BID). * differs by more than 20%."
  ), digits = 1)
```

```{r pknca_check}
nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(table_s4, -regimen, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("regimen", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(nca_med) == 9)
# AUC24,ss is dose / CL and is the structural check: a mis-transcribed CL/F,
# dose or unit moves it by tens of percent. Cmax adds V/F and KA. Cmin,ss is
# shown but not asserted: it sits in the far tail of a 4-h half-life and its
# median is dominated by the KA and V/F variability of the cohort.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_med$pct[nca_med$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]) < 20),
  all(abs(nca_med$pct[nca_med$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]) < 25)
)
```

AUC24,ss and Cmax,ss agree with Table S4. The simulated Cmin,ss medians
of the 300 mg once- and twice-daily regimens sit well above the Table S4
medians (flagged rows). Table S4 summarises empirical Bayes predictions, which
shrink KA and V/F towards the typical value for sparsely sampled patients,
whereas the virtual cohort draws the full IIV; with a 4-h half-life the trough
lies far down the elimination phase and is the metric most sensitive to that
difference and to the covariate mix of the cohort. Table S4 itself shows that
its regimens are different patient mixes: from 300 to 600 mg once daily its
median AUC24,ss doubles (8829 to 18354 ng*h/mL) but its median Cmin,ss
quadruples (13 to 52 ng/mL), which no linear one-compartment model can do for
a single population, whereas the virtual cohort gives every regimen the same
covariate distribution. The 600 mg once-daily trough agrees.

The individual exposures feed the exposure-response models:

```{r exposures}
expo <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  select(id, regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  transmute(id, regimen, AUC_SAVOLITINIB = auclast, CMAX = cmax, CTROUGH = cmin)
stopifnot(nrow(expo) == 3 * n_per_arm, all(expo$CTROUGH > 0))
```

# Exposure-efficacy: objective response (Figure 3)

The ORR models are logistic in the natural log of Cmin,ss, digitised from the
plotted curves. A logistic regression with an intercept, fitted by maximum
likelihood, predicts on average exactly the observed response rate of its own
data. The printed responder counts of each panel therefore test the digitised
intercept: the mean predicted probability over the virtual SAVANNAH-like
patients (the three combination regimens, equally weighted) should be close to
the observed rate. Because the slopes are shallow, the comparison is
insensitive to the exact exposure distribution.

```{r orr}
orr_models <- c(
  "All comers (3a)" = "Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_allcomers",
  "High biomarker (3b)" = "Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_highmet",
  "Low biomarker (3c)" = "Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_lowmet",
  "High biomarker, 2L (3d)" = "Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_orr_highmet_2l"
)
observed <- c(99 / 261, 87 / 174, 12 / 87, 67 / 126)
orr_eval <- function(model_name, ctrough) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(ctrough), time = 0, CTROUGH = ctrough)
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(model_name), d, returnType = "data.frame")$prob_orr
}
orr_check <- tibble(
  Subgroup = names(orr_models),
  observed = observed,
  predicted = vapply(orr_models, \(m) mean(orr_eval(m, expo$CTROUGH)), numeric(1))
)
knitr::kable(orr_check, digits = 3, caption = "Observed ORR (Figure 3 counts) vs mean predicted ORR over the virtual cohort.")
# Tolerance 0.05 absolute: the cohort is not SAVANNAH (regimen mix and
# covariates differ), but a misread intercept moves the mean by more.
stopifnot(all(abs(orr_check$predicted - orr_check$observed) < 0.05))

grid <- 10^seq(log10(0.7), log10(2500), length.out = 100)
bind_rows(lapply(names(orr_models), function(nm) {
  data.frame(Subgroup = nm, CTROUGH = grid, prob = orr_eval(orr_models[[nm]], grid))
})) |>
  ggplot(aes(CTROUGH, prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 17.3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~Subgroup) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Savolitinib Cmin,ss (ng/mL)", y = "Probability of objective response",
       caption = "Replicates the fitted curves of Shahraz 2026 Figure 3a-d.")
```

# Exposure-safety

## Probabilities printed in the Results (Figure 5)

The Results text prints the predicted probability of any related TEAE and of a
grade >= 3 related TEAE at the median and at the 5th and 95th percentile
exposure of each regimen; Table S4 gives those exposures. The four Figure 5
regressions were back-solved from these 36 values, so the table below checks
the transcription and shows how closely a linear logit reproduces them.

```{r fig5}
tab_s4_pct <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~pct, ~AUC_SAVOLITINIB, ~CMAX,
  "300 mg BID", "q05", 9768, 885, "300 mg BID", "median", 16220, 1346, "300 mg BID", "q95", 32091, 2088,
  "300 mg QD", "q05", 5394, 890, "300 mg QD", "median", 8829, 1376, "300 mg QD", "q95", 14997, 2043,
  "600 mg QD", "q05", 10881, 1445, "600 mg QD", "median", 18354, 2444, "600 mg QD", "q95", 37850, 3908
)
printed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint, ~metric, ~values,
  "any related TEAE", "AUC", c(.74, .76, .79, .74, .75, .76, .75, .76, .80),
  "any related TEAE", "Cmax", c(.74, .75, .76, .74, .75, .77, .75, .77, .79),
  "grade >= 3 related TEAE", "AUC", c(.21, .24, .29, .21, .22, .24, .22, .25, .31),
  "grade >= 3 related TEAE", "Cmax", c(.18, .21, .25, .20, .22, .25, .21, .26, .33)
)
safety_eval <- function(model_name, d) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(model_name), cbind(id = seq_len(nrow(d)), time = 0, d), returnType = "data.frame")
}
s_auc <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc", tab_s4_pct["AUC_SAVOLITINIB"])
s_cmax <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_cmax", tab_s4_pct["CMAX"])
fig5 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(printed)), function(i) {
  s <- if (printed$metric[i] == "AUC") s_auc else s_cmax
  col <- if (grepl("grade", printed$endpoint[i])) "prob_teae_drug_related_grade3" else "prob_teae_drug_related"
  tibble(tab_s4_pct[c("regimen", "pct")],
    endpoint = printed$endpoint[i], metric = printed$metric[i],
    printed = printed$values[[i]], model = s[[col]]
  )
}))
fig5 |>
  mutate(model = round(model, 3)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(endpoint, metric, regimen), names_from = pct, values_from = c(printed, model)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Printed probability (Results) vs packaged model at the Table S4 exposures.")
# Deterministic. The medians reproduce to within 0.007, all 36 values to
# within 0.015: the bracketed exposures used in the text may not be exactly
# the Table S4 percentiles (two Cmax values 5 ng/mL apart are printed as 0.18
# and 0.20), which no monotone curve can reproduce.
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig5) == 36,
  max(abs(fig5$model - fig5$printed)[fig5$pct == "median"]) < 0.008,
  max(abs(fig5$model - fig5$printed)) < 0.016
)
```

## The printed regressions and the plotted curves

Every supplementary panel prints its regression in the footnote and draws a
fitted curve. The two are not the same model. The printed regression is linear
in the exposure, and its Wald p-value is the one shown on the panel; the plotted
curve is a logistic regression in log(exposure), the fit a smoother produces on
a log-scaled axis. They agree near the middle of the exposure distribution and
diverge in the tails. The packaged models use the printed regressions. For
Figure S15a (grade >= 1 hepatotoxicity), the maintainers' fit to the plotted
curve is logit = -5.855 + 0.5348 * log(AUC24,ss):

```{r printed_vs_plotted, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
auc_grid <- 10^seq(log10(2500), log10(90000), length.out = 100)
heptox <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc", data.frame(AUC_SAVOLITINIB = auc_grid))
cmp_curves <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(AUC = auc_grid, prob = heptox$prob_hepatotoxicity, curve = "Printed regression (packaged)"),
  data.frame(AUC = auc_grid, prob = plogis(-5.855 + 0.5348 * log(auc_grid)), curve = "Plotted curve (digitised)")
)
ggplot(cmp_curves, aes(AUC, prob, linetype = curve)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Savolitinib AUC24,ss (ng*h/mL)", y = "P(grade >= 1 hepatotoxicity)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
# Near the centre of the data (10000 ng*h/mL) the two agree to 0.01.
stopifnot(abs(plogis(-5.855 + 0.5348 * log(1e4)) - plogis(-1.17 + 2.57e-5 * 1e4)) < 0.01)
```

Two panels have no footnote (Figures S14b and S28a) and are packaged from the
plotted curve, i.e. on the log scale; see Assumptions and deviations.

## All endpoints over the observed exposure range

```{r safety_curves, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
auc_curves <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc", data.frame(AUC_SAVOLITINIB = auc_grid))
cmax_grid <- 10^seq(log10(300), log10(6000), length.out = 100)
cmax_curves <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_cmax", data.frame(CMAX = cmax_grid))
long_curves <- bind_rows(
  auc_curves |> select(AUC_SAVOLITINIB, starts_with("prob_")) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-AUC_SAVOLITINIB, names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "prob") |>
    mutate(metric = "AUC24,ss (ng*h/mL)", x = AUC_SAVOLITINIB),
  cmax_curves |> select(CMAX, starts_with("prob_")) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-CMAX, names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "prob") |>
    mutate(metric = "Cmax,ss (ng/mL)", x = CMAX)
)
stopifnot(all(long_curves$prob >= 0 & long_curves$prob <= 1))
ggplot(long_curves, aes(x, prob, colour = metric)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ sub("^prob_", "", endpoint), ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Exposure", y = "Probability", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))
```

The paper reports two statistically significant (p < 0.001) positive
relationships: Cmax,ss with discontinuation (Figure S14b) and AUC24,ss with
grade >= 1 hepatotoxicity (Figure S15a). Both packaged slopes are positive.

```{r significant}
ini_cmax <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_cmax"))$iniDf
ini_auc <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc"))$iniDf
stopifnot(
  ini_cmax$est[ini_cmax$name == "e_logcmax_discont"] > 0.5,
  ini_auc$est[ini_auc$name == "e_auc_heptox"] > 2e-5
)
```

The virtual cohort's exposures give the expected incidence of each endpoint by
regimen:

```{r safety_cohort}
auc_cohort <- safety_eval("Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_auc", expo["AUC_SAVOLITINIB"])
auc_cohort$regimen <- expo$regimen
auc_cohort |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("prob_"), mean)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-regimen, names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "p") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = p) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean predicted probability by regimen, AUC24,ss models.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Race coding.** Table 1's footnote expands RACE (1) as Asian, but the
  Results state that Asian is the reference group and Figure 2 shows White as
  the only race whose exposure differs from the reference (AUC24,ss ratio
  0.827 = 1 / 1.212), with Asian, Black and Other at 1.00. The model therefore
  applies the RACE (1) effects to `RACE_WHITE`; the Figure 2 reproduction above
  confirms the coding.
* **Sex coding.** Data S1 writes the sex effects for SEX = 1 without naming the
  level; Figure 2 labels it female (AUC24,ss ratio 1.24 = 1 / 0.803).
* **Residual error.** Table 1 lists err_add and err_prop as thetas (theta4,
  theta5) and gives no CV, so they are taken as standard deviations (1.07
  ng/mL, 49.5%) of a combined error model; the table footnote's generic rule
  'CV% of sigma = sqrt(estimate)' is not applied to them.
* **Transit absorption.** Figure S3 names three absorption compartments
  (Tr0-Tr2) with every transfer at KA; the dose enters Tr0 (`depot`), so there
  are two transit compartments between the depot and the central compartment.
* **Covariates are baseline values.** Weight, bilirubin and alkaline
  phosphatase are baseline values (WT, BBILI, BALP); PPI use and osimertinib
  co-administration are subject-level in the source data.
* **ORR models are digitised from the plotted curves.** The paper prints no
  ORR regression. The curves are logistic in log(Cmin,ss) (RMS 0.002 on the
  probability scale). In the safety figures the plotted curves are of the same
  log form while the printed regressions are linear in exposure, so the
  regressions the authors used for the ORR inference may be linear in
  Cmin,ss; the two forms agree near the middle of the data. Use positive
  `CTROUGH` values.
* **Figure 5 regressions are back-solved.** The main-text Figure 5 panels have
  no footnote; the linear logits were fitted by least squares to the
  probabilities printed in the Results, read as the predictions at the median
  and the 5th and 95th percentile exposures of Table S4. The plotted Figure 5
  curves (log form) reproduce the printed medians less well than a linear
  logit does, consistent with the printed values coming from the linear
  regressions.
* **Two safety regressions are digitised on the log scale.** Figures S14b
  (discontinuation vs Cmax,ss) and S28a (grade >= 3 oedema vs AUC24,ss) lack
  the footnote, so the packaged coefficients reproduce the plotted curve, in
  log(exposure), unlike their 43 siblings. Their quartile event rates and the
  totals on the panels (138 and 30 events of 998) agree with the digitised
  curves.
* **Figure S20b is missing.** The published supplement reprints the Figure
  S17b panel (hypersensitivity vs Cmax,ss) in place of grade >= 3 pyrexia vs
  Cmax,ss, so `Shahraz_2026_savolitinib_safety_cmax` has no
  `prob_pyrexia_grade3`.
* **Exposure definition.** The paper derives each patient's exposures from the
  empirical Bayes estimates at the most prevalent dose. The AUC24,ss of a
  twice-daily regimen spans two dosing intervals.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates were drawn independently (no correlation
  between weight and sex, for example) from distributions matched to the
  pooled medians and interquartile ranges; Table S4 pools all 998 patients and
  all 13 regimens, so only the three regimens of interest are compared.
